simple.meaning: אַיִן (ʼayin) is a Hebrew object word meaning “where? (only in connection with prepositional prefix, whence).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 29:4. The surrounding context includes family.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַיִן (H370) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: Jacob said to them, “My relatives, where are you from?”
Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?”
Where could I get meat to give all these people? For they weep before me, saying, ‘Give us meat, that we may eat.’
The woman took the two men and hid them. Then she said, “Yes, the men came to me, but I didn’t know where they came from.
They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.”
Micah said to him, “Where did you come from?”
He lifted up his eyes, and saw the wayfaring man in the street of the city; and the old man said, “Where are you going? Where did you come from?”
He said, “If Yahweh doesn’t help you, where could I get help for you? From of the threshing floor, or from the wine press?”
Then Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah, and said to him, “What did these men say? From where did they come to you?”
Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?”
Where then does wisdom come from?
I will lift up my eyes to the hills.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah, and asked him, “What did these men say? From where did they come to you?”
Then they asked him, “Tell us, please, for whose cause this evil is on us. What is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your country? Of what people are you?”
It will happen that all those who look at you will flee from you, and say, ‘Nineveh is laid waste! Who will mourn for her?’ Where will I seek comforters for you?”

definitions.short: where? (only in connection with prepositional prefix, whence)
definitions.full: H370. ayin I. [ אַ֫יִן ] adverb (from אַי ; Assyrian aina , ainu , Arabic where? whence? ) only in the compound מֵאַ֫יִן 17 whence? Gen 29:4 ; 42:7 (synonym אֵימִֿזֶּה e.g. 16:8 ; 1Sam 30:13 ) Judg 17:9 ; 19:17 ; Job 1:7 ( 2:2 אֵימִֿזֶּה ); used in a rhetorical or poetic style (where אֵימִֿזֶּה would be too prosaic) Num 11:13 בָּשָׂר לִי מֵאַיִן whence have I flesh etc. ? 2Kin 6:27 ; Jer 30:7 Alas! for that day is great; כָּמוֺהוּ מֵאַיִן whence is its like ? (see also II. אַיִן near the end) Nahum 3:7 ; Psa 121:1 ; Job 28:12 , 20 ; in an indirect sentence Josh 2:4 (compare אֵימִֿזֶּה 1Sam 25:11 ). I. [ אַ֫יִן ], מֵאַ֫יִן whence? see below אַי
definitions.rootNote: probably identical with 369 in the sense of query (compare 336 )
